καιροῖς, ὅτε πολλὴ εὐφροσύνη καὶ ἱλαρότης ἦν ἐν αὐτοῖς, σπευδόντων ἐπὶ ἑορτὴν
τῶν ἁπανταχόθεν Ἰουδαίων ἐπὶ τὸ Σιὼν ὄρος. πολλῶν δὲ οὐσῶν τῶν πυλῶν τῶν
οἰκοδομηθεισῶν ἐν Σιὼν ἐκ πάντων τῶν κλιμάτων, φησὶν ὁ λόγος πάσας ἠφανίσθαι
, καὶ τοὺς ἱερεῖς στενάζειν , δηλονότι τὰ ἱερατικὰ ἔργα τὰ κατὰ τὰς ἑορτὰς καὶ τὰς
ἄλλας ἡμέρας οὐ δυναμένους ἐπιτελεῖν, ἤτοι τῷ ᾐχμαλωτίσθαι ἢ τῷ μηδένα εἶναι
τὸν προσιόντα αὐτοῖς καὶ τὰς λειτουργίας τὰς ἱε ρατικὰς ἀπαιτοῦντα. ἀλλὰ καὶ αἱ
παρθένοι , φησί, τῆς Σιὼν ἀγόμεναί εἰσι, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι ὑπὸ τῶν κεκρατηκότων
πολεμίων. 14 Πρὸς δὲ διάνοιαν· τῆς σκοπευτικῆς καὶ θεωρητικῆς δυνάμεως Σιὼν
καλουμένης πολλαὶ ὁδοί εἰσι τῶν ποικίλων δογμάτων, μυστι κῶν τε καὶ φυσικῶν
καὶ ἠθικῶν, τάχα δὲ καὶ λογικῶν, αἱ φέρουσαι ἐπὶ τὴν κατανόησιν καὶ θέαν τῶν
προκειμένων. ἐπὰν οὖν τις τὸ τούτων ἀσκητικὸν ἀπολέσας συγχυθῇ, πᾶσαι αὗται αἱ
ὁδοὶ πεν θοῦσιν οὐχ ὁδευόμεναι, πανηγύρεως μὲν ὑ
pass_a_gloss: When joy was high, Jews rushed to Zion's feast from all lands. Its many gates, built from every region, lie in ruins. Priests groan, unable to serve feast-day rites—either captive or without supplicants. Zion's virgins are led off by conquering foes. Zion, as the mind's contemplative power, holds many paths: mystical, physical, ethical, logical ways leading to insight and vision of set truths. If one abandons their discipline and falls into confusion, these paths wander untraveled, though festivals mark the known ways when walked and examined in order. But when deserted, they mourn, neither searching nor passing through, for the walkers have fallen, seized by passions, dragged to evil. Zion knows no sweetness, only inward bitterness. Do not read this bitterness as present anger. The word's clarity is this: some wished to afflict Judea, or were afflicting it, before captivity times. God defended Israel, yet they failed when aiding Him worthily. Later, they sinned—ignoring prophets, killing them—so enemies ruled them, helpless, as Symmachus says: their foes became chiefs. Some enemies, living among oppressors, thrived through cleverness or wealth, now subject to sinful Israel, humbled by God for countless wicked acts—so severe no infant spared, all driven into captivity by every oppressor. Leaders who rejoiced in Judah’s fall for breaking holy vows. We must clarify: Who is Zion’s daughter? What gives her beauty? What pasture do her rulers lack, like confused shepherds? How do the weak march toward their pursuer? We hold: Zion’s mountain is mother of her gathered people, called daughter Zion; her beauty is her clothing, seized by enemies during pasturing, taken from her. The world was taken away; synagogue leaders, pressed by enemies and captured, lacked kin and found no food like sheep. Weak rams, driven unfed, yield to pursuers; likewise captive leaders, led into captors' land, move weakly, seeming to the pursuer. Such a soul is Zion's daughter: as righteous daughter is righteous, wise daughter wise, so Zion's daughter is observant and theoretically examining. Her beauty and worth? Only the wealth of truth's holy doctrines, examined with wisdom. If one neglects beauty and worth after gaining them—losing continuity and divine increase—what the world has attained flows out and departs. Leaders guiding the word, attaining beauty, like rams' guides finding no flock pasture, establish scarcity, setting aside attention of helpers and flock, so I might say.
pass_b_english:
In those times when great joy and cheerfulness were among them, they hastened to the feast, gathering Jews from every place to Mount Zion. Many of the gates, which had been built in Zion from all the regions, the word says, have been utterly destroyed; and the priests are groaning, clearly because they are unable to perform the priestly duties prescribed for the feasts and the other days—either because they have been led into captivity, or because there is no one coming to them who seeks their priestly services and demands their ministrations. Moreover, the virgins of Zion, it is said, are being led away, and it is evident that they are taken by the victorious enemies. As for reflection: of Zion, called the contemplative and theorizing power, there are many ways of the diverse doctrines, mystical and physical and ethical, and perhaps also logical, which lead to the understanding and contemplation of the things set before us. Therefore, when one, having lost the disciplined practice of these things, becomes confused, all these ways wander without being traveled, though a festival exists along the previously mentioned ways, when they are walked, examined, and, as I might say, tread upon in order; but they mourn when they are deserted, neither inquiring nor passing through, because those who walk have fallen away and been taken captive by the passions, dragged about toward worse things. Zion, possessing nothing sweet anywhere, endures bitterness by itself. One must not take the present bitterness as being upon some kind of anger. The clarity of the word is such as this: they wished to afflict, or were afflicting, the Jewish land before the times of the captivity.

But they did not prevail, even while God was defending the Jews, when they offered themselves as worthy helpers. Yet when they sinned and, in addition to not listening to the prophets, even killed them—the sons of Israel—then they were handed over, helpless, to those who oppressed them, so that their enemies became their heads, as Symmachus has declared, rulers. Others, perhaps, who were enemies while living among the oppressors, either by invention or by substance, prospered in prosperity, having become subject to those who oppress, namely, those who remain behind due to their sins, whom the Lord has humbled because of the multitude of their godless deeds, even those who have transgressed and done this to such an extent that not even mercy is left for their infants, but they are led away into captivity, driven by every oppressor. Beginning with those who started and rejoiced in the Lord’s handing them over to humility because of the abundance of their godless deeds—those who had made covenants with the holy oracles toward Him but did not keep them. The power of these words must be made clear to us: they examine who is the daughter of Zion, and in what she possesses her beauty; what is the pasture, which the rulers of the daughter of Zion do not possess, like sheep owners bewildered about grazing; and how these, deprived of strength, go forward against the face of the one who pursues. But we consider that the mountain of Zion is indeed the mother of the assembly within her, the daughter called Zion; and the beauty of the daughter of Zion is her possession, the garments she wears, which possession, taken in the time of pasturing, was seized by the enemies and went forth from them.

Of these, the world was, that is, it was carried off (for this is a more emphatic way of saying it went out), and the leaders of the synagogue, because the enemies pressed upon them and took them captive, being at a loss for their kin, could not find nourishment like sheep. Just as rams, driven and not fed, go weakly forward, yielding to the force of those pursuing them, so also the leaders, having become captives, being led away into the land of those who took them captive, went forward not in strength, in appearance to the pursuer. But for understanding, such a soul is the daughter of Zion; just as the daughter of righteousness is the righteous one, and the daughter of wisdom is the wise one, so (since Zion is the place of observation) the observant and theoretically investigating daughter might be called Zion. What, then, could I rightly consider as her beauty and worth, except the wealth of the holy doctrines of truth, examined together with wisdom? Therefore, when someone neglects, after having attained beauty and worth, both the continuity of these things and the increase of the divine wealth, the things that as yet the world has attained flow out and depart. But the leaders, those who have guided the word and have managed to attain the aforementioned beauty, like rams, the guides, not finding pasture for the flock, have established themselves in scarcity, having set aside the attention of those who could help them and the flock, so that I might say,
